![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/90980bb04eb7dd9906ec9a99ea3a1b7cfd9c00969bbd9b12c60fe0f80eb88840.png)

The region enclosed by the curves $x+2{y}^{2}=1$ and $x=2{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi y}{3})$ for $y\in [-\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}]$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $x=1.$ Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
question.worked_solution:
First, since we are rotating about a vertical line, we need to solve the equation of our first curve for $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2{y}^{2} & =1\,⟹\,x=1-2{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/16ca1c96786eb8e7ef12608f70d03b34b679e63d34ef41135b4fd6801bcccc27.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $x=1-2{y}^{2},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $x=2{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi y}{3}).$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as a difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x=2{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi y}{3}).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/276dea7b2d9f50e3fe171cceb64c1c7a12f84cfb18bdbe242102802ad9790f49.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{-1/2}^{1/2}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1/2}^{1/2}{[\,(1)-(2{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi y}{3}))\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1/2}^{1/2}{[1-2{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi y}{3})]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1/2}^{1/2}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi y}{3})]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x=1-2{y}^{2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/b6c6fb140bb3eaf4c49cba76af157fb46a568bc2dc24e4763facede62720f844.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{-1/2}^{1/2}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1/2}^{1/2}{[\,(1)-(1-2{y}^{2})\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1/2}^{1/2}{[2{y}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1/2}^{1/2}({(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi y}{3}))}^{2}-{(2{y}^{2})}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1/2}^{1/2}({cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{2\pi y}{3})-4{y}^{4})\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
